content:
kevin: FYI we've got a customer escalation (ACME Corp) saying p95 latency is up from 120ms -> 400ms since 2026-03-12. Their dashboard shows the spike but our global SLO alert didn't fire. Can we triage?

maria: pulling traces now. Do we have the dashboard URL?

jen_support: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/ingress-latency?orgId=1&from=now-7d&to=now — customer pasted that in the ticket. They attached a curl to our API showing slower tail latencies vs last week.

kevin: thanks. my quick look: the dashboard uses a rollup metric (latency.request_ms) quantile aggregation in our metrics pipeline. The SLO alert uses the prometh->mimir quantile from the 1m rollup. Suspect bucket/aggregation mismatch.

olivia: can you paste the query used by the dash? sometimes the dashboard uses histogram_quantile on a raw histogram metric while alerts use the precomputed quantiles.

maria: dashboard panel shows:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))
```
Alert rule is:
```
avg_over_time(redwood_latency_p95{service="inference"}[5m]) > 0.25
```
alert uses the precomputed p95 timeseries produced by our aggregator (redwood_latency_p95).

raj: aha — different backends. histogram_quantile on the raw buckets vs precomputed p95 can diverge if the histogram buckets changed or if rollup windows differ. Any bucket changes recently?

nora: checking bucket release history — I found a change on 2026-03-11 where we compacted bucket boundaries to reduce cardinality: we moved from 40 to 20 buckets and switched to exponential bins for long-tail. Commit hash: a2b4f3c. That could skew histogram_quantile results.

kevin: that sounds like the smoking gun. The aggregator that produces redwood_latency_p95 samples quantiles from the pre-aggregation snapshots. If the dashboard computes quantiles from the new compacted buckets, the results won't match the old p95. The customer likely compared dashboards pre/post bucket change.

jen_support: customer insists they saw regression in actual API response times, not just dashboards. Any traces showing real latency?

maria: I pulled Jaeger traces for the customer tenant: spans show increased service time around 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC — but only for some requests hitting a specific model variant (quantized-v2).

olivia: so two issues: (1) instrumentation/metric bucket change causing dashboard vs alert mismatch, (2) a real performance regression for quantized-v2. We need to separate them—customer-facing mitigation first.

raj: mitigation plan: 1) revert bucket compaction for latency histograms for the next 24h (or enable a compatibility metric with old buckets) 2) add a temporary alert on raw histogram_quantile to catch true tail regressions 3) create a canary rollback for quantized-v2 if traces confirm perf hit.

kevin: Agree. Reverting buckets is a config change in metrics-pipeline. I'll open a PR to re-enable the previous bucket template for request_duration_seconds_bucket and deploy to staging, then canary to prod.

nora: For (2) I can add a long-term fix: publish both redwood_latency_p95 and redwood_latency_histogram_buckets_v1 so dashboards/alerts can be consistent. Also add a changelog entry and a migration guide for dashboard owners.

jen_support: I'll notify ACME that we're investigating and that we may update dashboards, and ask for any sample request IDs. They've provided 3 request IDs (rid: 93a, 93b, 93c).

maria: repro steps for the SLO mismatch we should document:
1) Query raw buckets: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))
2) Compare to precomputed p95: redwood_latency_p95{service="inference"}
3) Note divergence after 2026-03-11 when bucket template changed.

kevin: implementation notes: metrics-pipeline uses promrelayer that compacts histograms by mapping to a template. The template change reduced resolution for 100-500ms region. histogram_quantile is sensitive there. The precomputed p95 was computed using t-digest on raw samples before compaction — so values were more accurate pre-change.

olivia: Quick query I ran against prod (sampling customer tenant):
```
# raw hist quantile
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme"}[5m])) by (le))
# precomputed p95
redwood_latency_p95{tenant="acme"}
```
Result: raw hist jumped to ~410ms at 2026-03-12T03:22, precomputed p95 stayed ~130ms. Traces show some requests at ~380-420ms — so precomputed p95 underreports tail.

raj: why did precomputed p95 not capture the tail? It samples t-digest snapshots — did we change the sampling frequency?

nora: yes, another change: ingestion agent sampling rate decreased slightly around the same time to reduce load (commit b7f9d). That reduced t-digest fidelity for low-traffic tenants. Combined with compaction, tail gets smoothed out.

kevin: ops actions:
- Roll back bucket template (nora) — target: 1781002600 (in ~3 minutes)
- Temporarily increase sampling rate for t-digest for impacted tenants (maria)
- Add a one-off alert that uses histogram_quantile for tenant acme at 95th > 300ms to catch real regressions (olivia)
- Start a rollback of quantized-v2 if traces confirm it's the culprit (raj)

jen_support: ACME updated ticket: they need ETA and whether this affects SLAs. Any chance this was a billing-related config?

kevin: not billing. SLA impact: if the actual p95 is > our SLO threshold for >5m, we should trigger an incident. Since precomputed p95 missed it, we didn't fire. We should treat this as a metrics incident — root cause: metrics change + sampling change hid real regressions.

maria: I'm running the sampling increase now for tenants:acme and a small cohort. ping when done.

sre-bot: deploy started: metrics-pipeline revert-buckets (PR #3245) -> staging (user: kevin). Status: in-progress.

kevin: deploying canary buckets to prod in 2 phases: small region first. Will monitor both dashboards and raw traces.

nora: I've opened a ticket to add a pre-deploy checklist: any histogram template changes must include a compatibility flag and dashboard migration notes. Ticket RED-OPS-567.

olivia: added on-call playbook step: when p95/p99 diverge, do a quick check list: bucket changes, sampling changes, aggregator code changes, model variant deploys. Saving to playbook.

raj: update: traces indicate quantized-v2 increased mean CPU time by 20% on a small fraction of hosts due to a kernel microcode mismatch during the week. Not all requests affected. I'll coordinate with runtime team for a restart and hotfix.

kevin: good catch. So action items summary:
- kevin: finish bucket revert PR + canary deploy + monitor (ETA 30m)
- nora: add compatibility metric and docs (ETA 24h)
- maria: increase t-digest sampling for affected tenants (done)
- raj: coordinate runtime fix for quantized-v2 hosts and potential rollback (ETA 2h)
- olivia: add temporary histogram_quantile alert and update playbook (ETA 15m)
- jen_support: notify ACME with interim findings and ETA; gather more sample request IDs

jen_support: I'll post an interim update to ACME: we've identified two factors (metrics bucket change + a partial runtime regression on quantized-v2). We're rolling back the bucket change and increasing sampling to ensure alerts and dashboards align. We're actively investigating the runtime issue and will follow up within 2 hours. :pray:

maria: post-deploy check: after revert we should run an automated diff between histogram_quantile and redwood_latency_p95 over last 24h and produce a report. I can script that.

sre-bot: deploy success: metrics-pipeline revert-buckets -> prod (user: kevin). Duration: 4m.

kevin: monitor graphs now. Olivia, can you run the raw query again and paste numbers?

olivia: re-run: raw hist 95th for acme dropped back to ~135ms after revert. precomputed p95 matches ~130ms. The anomalous 400ms points for certain request IDs still present in traces — looks localized.

raj: started rolling restart of affected quantized-v2 hosts. Will report when the first batch is done.

kevin: closing the metrics mismatch for now. Keep this thread updated with runtime fix status. We'll do a postmortem once everything stabilizes and include migration guidance.

jen_support: Customer update sent. They replied: thanks for quick action, will wait for follow-up.

nora: I'll own the postmortem doc and link the PRs / commits (a2b4f3c, b7f9d). Will include repro steps and suggested dashboard queries that are robust to bucket template changes.

kevin: thanks everyone. If anyone finds more tenants affected, ping this thread.

olivia: quick note for dashboards owners: prefer querying raw histogram buckets with explicit bucket template label (if available) or use the precomputed quantile but ensure sampling/ingestion config is stable. We'll add explicit labels like bucket_template=v1 to avoid silent drift.

maria: tagging follow-up tasks in RED-ENG backlog.

sre-bot: incident closed: metrics-mismatch (severity: P2) — auto summary will be generated.
